full_name: OpenAI safety, alignment & preparedness teams (incl. Superalignment history)
mission: OpenAI's safety work is spread across alignment, safety-systems and preparedness teams; the Preparedness Framework (v2, Apr 2025) defines how it tracks capabilities that could cause severe harm and what safeguards must exist before deployment. The team history is turbulent: the Superalignment team (announced Jul 2023, led by Ilya Sutskever and Jan Leike, promised 20% of compute) was dissolved in May 2024 after both left; a 'Mission Alignment' team was disbanded in Feb 2026; in Jul 2026 safety was folded under Mia Glaese as VP of Research and Safety and head of safety systems Johannes Heidecke left. In Aug 2026 the FT reported the Preparedness team was disbanded; OpenAI denied this, saying its preparedness leads report to head of safety Saachi Jain. 'Founded' marks the Preparedness team / Superalignment launch year.

key_work.title: Introducing Superalignment
key_work.plain_summary: Announced a team to solve the alignment of superintelligent AI within four years, with 20% of OpenAI's compute; the team was dissolved in 2024.

key_work.title: Weak-to-strong generalization
key_work.plain_summary: Superalignment's first paper: tested whether a weak model can supervise a stronger one, as an analogy for humans supervising superhuman AI.

key_work.title: Our updated Preparedness Framework (v2)
key_work.plain_summary: Defines Tracked Categories (bio/chem, cyber, AI self-improvement) and two thresholds — High and Critical — with required safeguards reviewed by a Safety Advisory Group before deployment.

key_work.title: Deliberative alignment
key_work.plain_summary: Teaches reasoning models to recall and reason over written safety rules before answering, improving jailbreak resistance while reducing over-refusals.

key_work.title: Detecting misbehavior in frontier reasoning models
key_work.plain_summary: Showed that reading a reasoning model's chain of thought can catch reward hacking, but penalising 'bad thoughts' can teach models to hide them.

key_work.title: Detecting and reducing scheming in AI models (with Apollo Research)
key_work.plain_summary: Found behaviours consistent with scheming in controlled tests of frontier models and tested a training method that reduced covert actions.

size_note: Repeated leadership turnover: Superalignment dissolved 2024; Mission Alignment disbanded Feb 2026; safety folded into research Jul 2026; FT-reported Preparedness disbanding disputed by OpenAI (Aug 2026).

warnings.text: Capabilities in biology/chemistry, cybersecurity and AI self-improvement could create new pathways to severe harm (Preparedness Framework Tracked Categories).
Research Categories flagged as possible future severe risks: long-range autonomy, sandbagging (deliberately underperforming), autonomous replication, undermining safeguards, nuclear/radiological.
Superintelligence alignment is unsolved: 'we don't have a solution for steering or controlling a potentially superintelligent AI' (Superalignment announcement, 2023).
Pressuring a model's chain of thought can make it hide misbehaviour rather than stop it (CoT monitoring research).

recommendations.text: Systems reaching 'High' capability must have safeguards that sufficiently minimise severe risk before deployment; 'Critical' systems also need safeguards during development (Preparedness Framework v2).
Publish Capabilities Reports and Safeguards Reports reviewed by a cross-functional Safety Advisory Group before deployment decisions.
Build scalable automated evaluations so testing keeps pace with frequent model updates, plus expert deep dives.
'We recommend against applying strong optimization pressure directly to the CoTs of frontier reasoning models' — keep chain-of-thought monitorable (CoT monitoring post, 2025).
